definition: A square matrix with one row and one column for each vertex of a graph, whose entry in row $i$, column $j$ is the number of edges going directly from vertex $i$ to vertex $j$; it is symmetric when the graph is undirected.
A sequence of edges in which each edge starts at the vertex where the previous edge ended; vertices and edges may be repeated, and the length of the walk is the number of edges it uses.

A table with a row and a column for each vertex of a weighted graph, giving the weight (such as a cost, distance or time) of the direct edge from the row's vertex to the column's vertex, with a blank where there is no direct edge.
A square matrix of the probabilities of moving between states in one step; in IB notation $T_{ij}$ is the probability of moving from state $j$ to state $i$, so each column adds up to $1$.
